profile.campus: Google Central Ohio (New Albany / Columbus-Lockbourne / Lancaster), OH
profile.address: Morse Road, Oakland, Jefferson Township, Franklin County, OH 43054
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's New Albany-area, Ohio data center footprint, mapped on Morse Road in Oakland, Jefferson Township, Franklin County, and carries the informational label NBY-6 in this registry's underlying mapping data, not independently confirmed against a Google-published building index this session. Google's own Ohio locations page, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within this footprint.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own Ohio data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the company broke ground in New Albany in 2019 and has since invested more than $20 billion in the state across New Albany, Lancaster, and Columbus, generating $21.7 billion in Ohio economic activity in 2025 and contributing over $16 million in philanthropic giving since 2006.

Ohio's central corridor data center cluster, of which this building is part, has grown rapidly since 2019 alongside major campuses for Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services, all separately tracked in this registry, though Google's own public materials describe its Ohio footprint in aggregate rather than naming individual buildings, addresses, or per-building capacity figures.

American Electric Power (AEP Ohio) is the principal electric utility serving most of the New Albany and Columbus-area data center market, and has filed with Ohio regulators for new large-load electric tariff structures in response to rapidly growing data center demand in the corridor. New Albany's community authority has used tax-increment financing agreements, and Ohio's state-level data center sales and use tax abatement program, to help anchor the cluster's continued growth alongside Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services campuses tracked elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
Google does not publish power capacity, square footage, or individual building specifications for NBY-6, treating facility-level disclosure as outside its policy even though the company reports aggregate investment figures at state and regional level. The site is part of a multi-county Columbus-area campus where Google has committed $1.7 billion across new facilities in Franklin, Licking, and Fairfield counties, positioning it alongside AWS and Meta as a major hyperscale investor in the same corridor.

Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities, but only 8 publish power capacity figures totaling 60.4 MW. Without published specifications for NBY-6, its contribution to the state's disclosed capacity cannot be calculated and its rank among Ohio sites reflects an incomplete registry rather than a measure of actual scale. The facility's location in Franklin County places it within the active New Albany investment zone rather than in an isolated or constrained region.

To assess whether NBY-6 matters to AI scaling, a reader would need to infer from Google's $1.7 billion regional investment and the known density of hyperscale construction in this corridor, since the operator's disclosure policy excludes the power and configuration data that would allow direct comparison to other campuses. The facts published here establish only that the facility exists, is part of a significant regional investment, and that capacity details remain proprietary.
